languages.name: C
languages.description: C systems programming reference focused on memory, ABI-level data, files, compilation, and interoperability.

categories.name: Core Language
categories.description: Types, control flow, functions, and translation units.

entries.title: Fundamental types
entries.summary: Use integer, floating, character, and boolean-like fundamental C types.
entries.definition: Use integer, floating, character, and boolean-like fundamental C types.
entries.mental_model: C types describe raw value representation and operations.

examples.title: Example

entries.title: if / switch
entries.summary: Choose control-flow branches using conditions or integral-like cases.
entries.definition: Choose control-flow branches using conditions or integral-like cases.

examples.title: Example

entries.title: for / while loops
entries.summary: Repeat statements using counter- or condition-driven loops.
entries.definition: Repeat statements using counter- or condition-driven loops.

entries.title: Functions
entries.summary: Define callable procedures with typed parameters and return values.
entries.definition: Define callable procedures with typed parameters and return values.
entries.mental_model: A typed call boundary with value/pointer arguments.

examples.title: Example
examples.code: int add(int a, int b) { return a + b; }

entries.title: Header files
entries.summary: Declare interfaces shared across translation units.
entries.definition: Declare interfaces shared across translation units.
entries.mental_model: Headers are textual interface fragments included before compilation.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
/* mathx.h */
int add(int a, int b);
examples.explanation: Declares a function in a header.

entries.title: static and extern
entries.summary: Control linkage/storage duration and declare externally defined symbols.
entries.definition: Control linkage/storage duration and declare externally defined symbols.
entries.mental_model: Linkage determines whether names cross translation-unit boundaries.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
static int internal_count;
extern int shared_count;
examples.explanation: Defines an internal symbol and declares an external one.

categories.name: Pointers and Memory
categories.description: Addresses, arrays, strings, allocation, and lifetime.

entries.title: Pointers
entries.summary: Store memory addresses and dereference them with *.
entries.definition: Store memory addresses and dereference them with *.
entries.mental_model: A pointer is a typed numeric-like reference to memory.

examples.title: Example
examples.explanation: Reads a value through its address.

entries.title: Arrays
entries.mental_model: Contiguous elements with no built-in runtime bounds checking.

entries.title: C strings
entries.summary: Represent text as char arrays terminated by a zero byte.
entries.definition: Represent text as char arrays terminated by a zero byte.
entries.mental_model: String boundaries are encoded by a sentinel byte, not stored length.

entries.title: malloc / free
entries.summary: Allocate and release dynamic heap memory manually.
entries.definition: Allocate and release dynamic heap memory manually.
entries.mental_model: You manually pair resource acquisition with release.
entries.gotchas: Leaks, double-free, and use-after-free are programmer hazards.

examples.title: Example
examples.explanation: Allocates and frees an integer array.

entries.title: struct
entries.summary: Group named fields into one aggregate type.
entries.definition: Group named fields into one aggregate type.
entries.mental_model: Named fields laid out in memory with possible padding.

examples.title: Example
examples.code: struct Macro { const char *key; const char *language; };

entries.title: function pointers
entries.summary: Store addresses of functions with compatible signatures.
entries.definition: Store addresses of functions with compatible signatures.
entries.mental_model: Behavior represented as an address with a signature contract.

examples.title: Example
examples.explanation: Calls a function through a pointer.

categories.name: I/O and Compilation
categories.description: Files, errors, macros, and the compile/link model.

entries.title: FILE* I/O
entries.summary: Use stdio streams for file input and output.
entries.definition: Use stdio streams for file input and output.
entries.mental_model: stdio wraps file descriptors/handles with buffered stream behavior.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
FILE *f = fopen("out.txt", "w");
if (f) { fputs("Wyn\n", f); fclose(f); }

entries.title: errno
entries.summary: Inspect thread-local error codes used by many C/POSIX APIs.
entries.definition: Inspect thread-local error codes used by many C/POSIX APIs.
entries.mental_model: A side-channel error number set by certain failing APIs.

entries.title: Preprocessor macros
entries.summary: Perform token-level transformations before C compilation.
entries.definition: Perform token-level transformations before C compilation.
entries.mental_model: The preprocessor rewrites tokens before the compiler sees C.

entries.title: Compilation and linking
entries.summary: Compile source into object files, then link objects/libraries into an executable.
entries.definition: Compile source into object files, then link objects/libraries into an executable.
entries.mental_model: Translation units become objects; the linker resolves symbols between them.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
cc -c main.c -o main.o
cc main.o -o app
examples.explanation: Builds an executable in two stages.

entries.title: Undefined behavior
entries.summary: Certain invalid operations have no defined C semantics, allowing arbitrary results.
entries.definition: Certain invalid operations have no defined C semantics, allowing arbitrary results.
entries.mental_model: The standard stops promising what happens, so optimizers may assume it never occurs.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
int *p = NULL;
/* *p = 1; would invoke undefined behavior */
examples.explanation: Shows a null pointer that must not be dereferenced.
